findings.title: The minute firing is not stopped until `mt-run` returns
findings.description: `run()` calls `subprocess.run` synchronously, and `mt-run minute` follows the systemd unit until it exits. The journal polling that detects `TRAILING_COMPLETE` therefore starts only after the firing has finished; an unbounded backfill can keep the cutover waiting for hours or longer instead of stopping the service at the trailing-phase marker. Start the unit without blocking, or otherwise monitor the journal while the launcher is running.

findings.title: The repair subprocess is not authorized by the supplied sudoers rules
findings.description: `_repair()` invokes the production Python interpreter directly with `sudo`, but `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops` permits root commands only through the listed systemctl, `mt-run`, installer, and `cat` aliases (lines 7–13). Under the documented operator invocation, the repair check/apply/verify commands will be denied, so the cutover cannot complete with these permissions installed. Permit the narrowly scoped repair invocation or route it through an already-authorized command.

findings.title: A failed verification can be counted as successful
findings.description: `_repair()` records a nonzero return code but returns only the captured text. The cutover later determines acceptance by searching for `FAIL` and `[WAIT]`; for example, `--verify` can exit with `scan refused` before printing either marker, and that output can therefore satisfy the acceptance checks. Preserve and check the subprocess exit status, and fail closed when verification does not exit successfully.

findings.title: The sudoers rule grants broader access than the cutover needs
findings.description: `MT_RUN` allows any arguments to `/usr/local/bin/mt-run`, and that wrapper sends non-wrapper verbs to the production `mt` CLI. This gives the operator passwordless root execution of arbitrary CLI commands, not just the minute and daily pass commands used by this cutover. Restrict the permitted arguments to the required operations.

findings.title: The changed acquisition path lacks a realistic load test
findings.description: The daemon now performs a universe-wide truncated-session scan and adds a session-bounds database query for each fetched chunk. The added unit tests exercise behavior with mocks, while the load test in this change set measures the separate session-mass health query; none exercises this network/database acquisition path with a realistic universe or asserts latency/resource bounds. The review rules require a gated load test for changes on these paths.
